_comment: DERIVED artifact — not upstream bytes. Per-message JSON key allowlists and enum ranges transcribed from the .proto files of the pinned opentelemetry-proto release recorded in OTLP_PROTO_VERSION (see README.md for the exact source URLs and the transcription rule). Field names here are the lowerCamelCase forms the OTLP/JSON encoding mandates; the protos declare them in snake_case. The conformance validator reads THIS file rather than hardcoding the schema in Go, so re-pinning a newer release is a data change plus a re-transcription, never a silent code drift. Producer rule: an emitted key absent from its message's allowlist is a violation (a typo'd field name is silently discarded by a conformant receiver, which is exactly the class of defect that ships unnoticed). This is distinct from the receiver-side rule that unknown fields MUST be ignored.

KeyValue.source: common/v1/common.proto L77-97 — keyStrindex is Profiling-only and mutually exclusive with key; allowlisted for completeness of the transcription, never emitted by this producer

hex_id_fields._comment: field name -> required decoded byte width. Values are case-insensitive hex strings, NOT base64 (spec deviation 1). 16 bytes = 32 hex chars, 8 bytes = 16 hex chars.

_decimal_string_comment: 64-bit integers (fixed64/int64) are encoded as JSON decimal STRINGS by proto3 JSON mapping. A bare JSON number here is the single most common Go mistake, because encoding/json emits a number for int64/uint64 unless the field carries the string option.
_json_number_comment: uint32/fixed32/enum fields are JSON NUMBERS, not strings. Over-applying the decimal-string rule to these is the mirror-image mistake.

http.source: docs/specification.md — OTLP/HTTP Request; both are stated as MUST/default at the pinned tag
